previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and chronic pelvic pain was admitted for acute-on-chronic left lower quadrant abdominal pain, identical to prior flares. Despite recent hospitalization and initiation of indomethacin, her pain remained uncontrolled. Workup including pelvic and abdominal ultrasounds showed no acute pathology, and infections were ruled out. She was managed with IV fluids for hypokalemia, pain control with IV and oral opioids, and medication adjustments per pain team recommendations. Tachycardia resolved with hydration and pain relief. Subclinical hypothyroidism was noted, likely lithium-induced, and anemia improved without intervention. She was discharged home with optimized pain regimen, follow-up plans, and instructions to complete a colonoscopy prior to surgical evaluation.
